summary: 좋아하는 영화 장르(sci-fi) 설명하기. 튜터 평가: 질문 이해 완벽, 'ambiguous' 사용으로 어휘 만점. film vs movie 차이, go to the movies / catch a flick / matinee 등 영화 관련 표현 배움.

upgrades.said: I watched a movie which title is Hope
upgrades.better: I watched a movie called Hope
upgrades.note_ko: 'titled/which title is'는 딱딱하고 어색해요. 원어민은 그냥 called를 써요.

upgrades.said: I enjoy watching movie
upgrades.better: I enjoy watching movies
upgrades.note_ko: 영화 전반을 말할 땐 복수형. 바로 다음 문장에선 스스로 맞게 말했어요.

upgrades.said: I usually go to movie theater to watch movies
upgrades.better: I usually go to the movies
upgrades.note_ko: 관사 누락 + 원어민은 'go to the movies'가 제일 자연스러워요.

upgrades.said: it is like somewhat ambiguous thing
upgrades.better: it was pretty ambiguous
upgrades.note_ko: somewhat은 격식체·문어체 → kinda/pretty. '~한 것(thing)' 직역도 빼요.

upgrades.said: I couldn't understand what the movie's content is
upgrades.better: I didn't really get what it was about
upgrades.note_ko: '내용' 직역 함정. 영화 내용은 what it's about, 이해하다는 get이 자연스러워요.

upgrades.said: I found some reviews
upgrades.better: I looked up some reviews
upgrades.note_ko: found는 우연히 발견한 느낌. 일부러 찾아본 건 look up.

upgrades.said: after I found that, I can understand what the movie is
upgrades.better: and then it finally clicked
upgrades.note_ko: '그제야 이해됐다'는 it clicked가 딱이에요. 과거 얘기는 시제도 과거로.

upgrades.said: It is very wonderful experience to me
upgrades.better: It was a really cool experience
upgrades.note_ko: 과거 시제 + 관사 a 필요. wonderful보다 cool/great이 캐주얼해요.

upgrades.said: What source is good to me to learn English
upgrades.better: Do you know any good YouTube channels for learning English?
upgrades.note_ko: good/helpful은 'for me'예요 (to me 아님). 추천 요청 문장은 통으로 외워두면 좋아요.

feedback_ko: 발음·이해력은 좋다는 평가. 교정 포인트: ① -ed 발음을 한 음절로 (watched를 watch-it처럼 두 음절로 말하지 않기) ② 관사 a/the 습관적 누락 ③ good/helpful + for me ④ 격식체 어휘(somewhat, titled)를 캐주얼하게 (kinda, called). 튜터가 폰·자막을 영어로 바꾸는 환경 세팅을 추천했고, 다음 시간에 유튜브 채널을 추천해주기로 함.

script_en.text: Hi! How are you doing? Are you ready for class? Great — textbook, Lesson 9: movies. You indicated that you like going to the movies. What's your favorite genre, and why do you like it?

Well, I love watching movies — I go to the movies pretty often. My favorite genre is sci-fi, because I love imagining what's going on behind the story. For example, a few days ago I watched a Korean movie called Hope. When it ended, I didn't really get what it was about — it was pretty ambiguous. So I looked up some reviews and interviews with the actors and the director, and then it finally clicked. That was a really cool experience, so I love that kind of movie a lot.

Good job — you understood the question perfectly, and your pronunciation was good. One thing: 'watched' is one syllable, not 'watch-it.' Pretty much any word ending in -ed blends together — watched, learned.

Vocabulary — great use of the word 'ambiguous.' That's a 10. Grammar: you said 'I enjoy watching movie' once, then said it right — it's 'movies,' because we're talking about more than one. Remember your articles too: 'I go to a movie theater to watch a movie.' And instead of 'the film is titled Hope,' just say 'the movie is called Hope' — 'is titled' isn't incorrect, but it sounds stiff.
What's the difference between 'film' and 'movie'?

There's no real difference. I'd say 90% of Americans say 'movie.' People who went to college, or who think of movies as art, say 'film.' Movies are entertainment — like Spider-Man; film is art. I have a film degree, and I called them movies until I started college. People who just watch movies for fun don't call them films.

Also, Americans say 'going to the movies,' while British people say 'going to the cinema' — they don't really say 'movie theater.' There's slang too: a 'flick.' You want to catch a flick? It comes from the projector light flickering on the screen. Some people also say 'a show' — we're going to the show.

And there are time words too: a 'matinee' is a movie that shows in the afternoon. It's originally a French word meaning 'morning' — English borrowed it in the 19th century for daytime shows. If you see a movie around 11 or 12, you'd say, 'We're going to see a matinee.'
Can I ask something? Do you know any good YouTube channels for learning English?
I can't answer right now, but I'll look for some resources during my break and put three or four channels in your notes. YouTube definitely helps — I use it for Spanish myself.

Also, little things you can do: change your phone settings to English, keep English subtitles on even when you're watching something in Korean, and change your TV and Siri too. Surround yourself with the language as much as you can, especially if you're not in an English-speaking environment.
I've always heard you should find videos you're actually interested in, but I don't know which channels would work for me.
I'll find you some channels. Talk to you next class!

summary: 프리토킹 15분. 회사에서 포지션이 바뀐 이야기, 이번 주말 동료 결혼식과 축의금, 한국 vs 미국 결혼식(미국은 예식 후 DJ·춤 파티), 쌀쌀해진 날씨와 옷 쇼핑. 튜터 피드백: at my company, confused vs confusing(-ed/-ing), by himself, be동사 누락.

upgrades.said: big change on my company
upgrades.better: a big change at my company
upgrades.note_ko: 회사·장소는 at (튜터 교정).

upgrades.said: It's a little bit confused and frustrated
upgrades.better: It was kinda confusing and frustrating
upgrades.note_ko: 상황이 주는 감정은 -ing, 내가 느끼는 감정은 -ed (I was confused). 튜터가 가장 길게 설명한 포인트.

upgrades.said: I just got report about the position change
upgrades.better: I just found out about it
upgrades.note_ko: '통보받다' 직역. 소식을 알게 된 건 found out.

upgrades.said: my position has been changed
upgrades.better: I got moved to a different position
upgrades.note_ko: 현재완료 수동태는 보고서 톤. 나한테 일어난 일은 got + p.p.가 캐주얼해요.

upgrades.said: it is somewhat not bad now
upgrades.better: it's actually not that bad now
upgrades.note_ko: somewhat은 문어체 (8/5 리포트 포커스). 'not that bad'를 통째로.

upgrades.said: I want to handle something more trendy
upgrades.better: I wanted to work on newer tech
upgrades.note_ko: '다루다' 직역 → 업무는 work on. trendy의 비교급은 trendier.

upgrades.said: because of my partner didn't finish the job
upgrades.better: because my partner couldn't finish the job
upgrades.note_ko: because of + 명사 / because + 문장.

upgrades.said: I have to move to this position for helping him
upgrades.better: I had to go back to help him
upgrades.note_ko: '~하기 위해'는 to + 동사 (for -ing ✗). 지난 일이니 had to.

upgrades.said: he can't finish that project on himself
upgrades.better: he couldn't finish the project by himself
upgrades.note_ko: '혼자서' = by himself / on his own (튜터 교정).

upgrades.said: in my own thoughts, he didn't try harder as much
upgrades.better: Honestly, I don't think he tried that hard
upgrades.note_ko: '내 생각엔' 직역 → Honestly, I think / If you ask me.

upgrades.said: if he tried to finish that project harder, I can admit it
upgrades.better: if he'd really tried, I'd get it
upgrades.note_ko: 사실과 반대인 가정이면 can이 아니라 would. he'd tried = he had tried.

upgrades.said: I have to do that job, the replace of him
upgrades.better: I end up doing it for him
upgrades.note_ko: '그 사람 대신' = for him / instead of him. end up -ing = 결국 ~하게 되다.

upgrades.said: the wedding ceremony of my coworker
upgrades.better: my coworker's wedding
upgrades.note_ko: A of B보다 B's A가 구어적. ceremony는 보통 생략.

upgrades.said: she's my very familiar companion
upgrades.better: We're really close.
upgrades.note_ko: familiar = 낯익은, companion = 문어. 친하다 = close, 동료 = coworker.

upgrades.said: the basic price is about $80
upgrades.better: people usually give around 80 bucks
upgrades.note_ko: price는 물건값. 축의금 액수는 the usual amount / people usually give ~.

upgrades.said: she married with the American guy
upgrades.better: she married an American guy
upgrades.note_ko: marry는 with 없이 바로 사람. 처음 언급이니 an.

upgrades.said: they reserve some place and just take a party
upgrades.better: they rented a venue and just threw a party
upgrades.note_ko: take a party ✗ → have / throw a party.

upgrades.said: it's very very great
upgrades.better: it's really nice out
upgrades.note_ko: great엔 very를 잘 안 붙여요. 날씨는 nice out.

upgrades.said: it is a little bit little bit cold
upgrades.better: it's getting kinda chilly
upgrades.note_ko: chilly = 쌀쌀한. a little bit 반복 → kinda / a bit.

upgrades.said: some clothes for preparing autumn and winter
upgrades.better: some fall and winter clothes
upgrades.note_ko: '준비하기 위해' 직역. 미국은 autumn보다 fall.

upgrades.said: she a bit nervous
upgrades.better: she's a little nervous
upgrades.note_ko: be동사 누락 (튜터 교정).

feedback_ko: 프리토킹 15분 동안 대화가 끊기지 않았고, 모르는 단어(snore)는 돌려 말해서 튜터한테 받아냄. 'Not at all', 'It's not bad' 같은 짧은 리액션 좋음. 교정 포인트: ① 전치사 — at my company, at the workshop, by himself, marry(전치사 X) ② -ed/-ing 감정 형용사 — confused vs confusing, bored vs boring ③ 한국어 명사 직역 — companion(동료→coworker), familiar(친한→close), report(통보→found out), basic price ④ somewhat·a little bit 반복 → kinda/pretty ⑤ 지난 일 현재형으로 말하기(I want → I wanted).

script_en.text: Hi! How are you doing? Are you ready for class? Would you like a free talk class or a textbook class?
Free talk, please.
Wonderful. How's your week going?

Actually, there's been a big change at my company. While I was at a workshop, I found out I'd been moved back to my old position. So it was kinda confusing and frustrating at first. But now that I'm back, it's actually not that bad.
Oh, okay. Good thing, bad thing? What are you doing that's different?
So, I used to work on one AI model, and then I switched to an image-editing model — that's newer tech, and it's kinda hot right now. But now I'm back on my old project, which uses older tech.
Got you — so the technology you're working with is a little older. How do you feel about it? Are you glad, do you not care, or are you excited about the new chance?
Honestly, I'm not too happy about it. I switched because I wanted to work on newer tech. But my old partner couldn't finish his project by himself, so I had to go back and help him out.
Oh, that's too bad. Did they tell you why they moved you?

Yeah — the guy I worked with on the older project couldn't finish it on his own, so I have to help him wrap it up. I mean, if he'd really been trying, I'd get it. But honestly, I don't think he tried that hard. So I kinda end up doing his part for him.
That's not cool. All right — do you have any plans for this weekend?
Not much going on. I've just got a coworker's wedding to go to, this Sunday.
Oh nice! Are you excited about the wedding?
Yeah, we're really close. I actually saw her today, right before her big day.
Is she excited?
She's a little nervous — she's worried she'll forget something or mess something up.
Are you going to give her money for the wedding? How much do you have to give?
Yeah, in Korea you usually give cash. People usually give around 80 bucks.
Interesting! Weddings in Korea are pretty short, though. You don't dance or anything after?
No, not at all. No dancing and no after-party.
That doesn't sound fun! What's a wedding without dancing? You guys just eat dinner and go home. Have you ever been to a wedding from another culture?

Not yet. But a friend of mine lives in the US now — she married an American guy. She had an American-style wedding and sent me some photos. It looked so different from weddings here — they just rented a venue and threw a party.

Yeah, that's exactly what it is. The wedding itself is very formal, but then you go to another place, and there's a DJ or a band, a lot of alcohol, and everyone just dances. It's a lot of fun. How's the weather? I hear it's lovely in Korea right now.
Yeah, it's really nice out. But it's getting kinda chilly.
Do you have any other plans this weekend besides the wedding?
Oh yeah, I need to go shopping for some fall and winter clothes.
How often do you go shopping for food? Every few days, or once a week?
Honestly, I barely ever go grocery shopping. I eat all my meals at work — breakfast, lunch, and dinner.
I heard the food there is good, right?
It's not bad!
What do you have at home if you get hungry in the middle of the night?
Just some snacks or fruit.

Okay, let's go over some English. Instead of 'a big change on my company,' say 'at my company.' Also, 'confused' is how we feel — 'I'm confused,' 'I'm bored.' When something makes us feel that way, we use -ing. So the situation at your job isn't confused — it's confusing. If I say 'my girlfriend is bored,' that's how she feels. But 'my girlfriend is boring' means she makes me feel bored — you could get in trouble mixing those up!

And instead of 'on himself,' say 'by himself' — he couldn't do the job by himself. Don't forget your 'is,' too: 'she is a little bit nervous,' not 'she a bit nervous.' Besides that, you did good. I put all of that in your notes. Talk to you next week!
